answer: I pick a provenance-gated registration kernel: a new agent joins only if a verified sponsor vouches for it and stakes funds slashed when that node misbehaves. Sponsors face a hard cap on children and lose standing per failed spawn, so one attacker cannot cheaply fan out a fleet. Each seat also pays a per-epoch fee that climbs with cluster size, making cost superlinear. On an open horizon, a thousand fake personas would need a thousand real stakes plus fees, all forfeitable on the first coordinated lie, far above any epoch's reward. A jade seal carried the same idea: trust expensive to fake.
